summary: OnyxBank: multipath retry amplification causing duplicate completions, latency spike, and invoice exposure — post-incident action plan
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC a subset of OnyxBank traffic routed through the realtime-router experienced a multipath retry amplification. Requests that normally fan out to 1-2 serving backends were duplicated across 6-10 backends due to stale routing metadata and an aggressive retry policy. Symptoms included elevated tail latency (p95 -> 18s), a surge of duplicate completions returned to the customer, streaming disconnects for long-running sessions, and a notable invoice delta reported by OnyxBank.

Impact:
- Customer-facing failures: intermittent streaming truncation and duplicate completions for 12% of OnyxBank requests between 14:12–15:25 UTC.
- Latency: sustained p95 increase from 400ms to 18s during peak amplification.
- Billing: OnyxBank reported a 3.7x unexpected token/billing delta for the affected window.
- Business: Enterprise SLA exposure and escalated executive contact.

Timeline (UTC):
- 14:08: OnyxBank reports increased errors to #support channel.
- 14:12: Alerts from routing service (error-rate, retries) trigger PagerDuty.
- 14:18: Triage confirms duplicate completions pattern; mitigation steps initiated.
- 14:25: Temporary rate-limiter rule applied to OnyxBank route; duplicate completions reduced by 60%.
- 14:42: Canary rollback of recent routing policy change (PR #2834) confirmed.
- 15:05: Autoscaler throttle engaged to protect global serving pools.
- 15:25: Normal routing behavior restored for OnyxBank.
- 15:40: Customer notified of resolution and temporary credit plan discussed.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Apply the exact routing policy merge from PR #2834 in a staging cluster with multiplexed fanout enabled.
2) Replay a burst of OnyxBank-like requests with high socket churn and intentionally delayed ack from 2nd-tier serving nodes.
3) Observe retry loop when routing metadata contains inconsistent 'preferred_backends' TTL across the router pool.

Logs / Metrics / Artifacts:
- Router logs: /var/log/realtime-router/2026-03-10/route-errors.log (sampled snippets pasted below).
- Trace: trace-id: 0a9f-onyx-14: link to trace in APM: https://apm.redwood.internal/traces/0a9f-onyx-14
- Dashboard: routing-retries/p95 and billing/token-usage dashboards (links attached in linked assets).

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis pointed to a misbehaving serving-host causing clients to retry. Sampling showed identical request IDs duplicated by the router itself.
- Root cause traced to a recent routing control-plane change that introduced a race: metadata TTL updates for 'preferred_backends' were applied asynchronously and a goroutine-level cache allowed stale values to persist for up to 45s under high churn.
- The router's retry policy default (max_retries=3 with aggressive backoff reset) combined with the stale metadata caused the same request to be sent repeatedly to multiple backends before successful ack.
- Billing exposure occurred because duplicate completions were accepted by OnyxBank's aggregator and counted as separate completions in token accounting.

Immediate fixes performed:
- Rolled back PR #2834 at 14:42 UTC (reverted control-plane behavior to synchronous metadata apply in the critical path).
- Applied an emergency soft-rate-limit for OnyxBank routes to cap concurrent fanout to 2 backends at 14:25 UTC.
- Disabled aggressive retry resets in router config (max_retries=1) for enterprise-tier routes at 14:30 UTC.
- Issued hotfix to router cache invalidation to reduce stale TTL window from 45s to 5s (deployed 14:56 UTC, promoted 15:12 UTC).

Workarounds for customer:
- Instructed OnyxBank to enable idempotency tokens on long-running conversational transactions to collapse duplicate completions on their side.
- Provided a temporary client-side retry guidance doc and recommended enabling server-sent deduplication heuristics.

Customer communication and escalation:
- OnyxBank CSM (Daniel Ortega) escalated to support at 14:10 UTC.
- Support provided rolling updates via #support channel and scheduled an executive-to-executive call at 16:00 UTC.
- Offered provisional invoice credit covering the affected 6-minute amplification window plus a 10% goodwill credit for SLA exposure.

Root cause (concise):
A race in the routing control-plane metadata propagation combined with an aggressive router retry policy resulted in request fanout amplification and duplicate completions which were counted by billing.

Resolution and verification steps:
- Control-plane rollback validated that router logs no longer show duplicate request IDs.
- Post-fix synthetic traffic and customer traffic show p95 latency returned to baseline and no duplication observed for 48 hours.
- Billing reconciliation indicates a 3.6x reduction of the anomalous tokens once deduplication and rate limits applied.

Follow-up actions (owner & due dates):
- (ENG-AP) Implement stronger metadata write-through guarantees in control-plane: owner Marco Ruiz, due 2026-04-02.
- (ENG-ROUTER) Add router-side request-id dedupe window and idempotency enforcement: owner Samira Patel, due 2026-03-24.
- (SRE) Add canary gating rule for routing policy merges with churn-level simulation: owner Kevin Osei, due 2026-03-31.
- (CS/Finance) Finalize billing credit and reconciliation with OnyxBank: owner Priya Kapoor, due 2026-03-17.
- (DOCS) Update customer-facing retry guidance and SDK examples: owner DevRel (Michael Liu), due 2026-03-20.

Post-incident retrospective notes:
- We lacked an automated pre-merge simulation that replays high-churn traffic patterns against routing config changes.
- The default router retry settings are too aggressive for enterprise routes that can trigger billing exposure.
- Need clearer cross-team ownership tags for control-plane changes that affect runtime invariants.

Lessons for on-call and support:
- For enterprise customers with billing sensitivity, prioritize soft-rate-limits and idempotency enforcement as the first mitigation path.
- Escalate to ENG lead within 20 minutes if duplicate request patterns are observed in router logs.

Resolution summary for customer-facing communication:
- Root cause identified and rolled back. Hotfix deployed to reduce stale routing metadata propagation and to cap retry-induced fanout.
- We will issue a billing credit for the affected window and follow up with a concrete prevention timeline.

Attached/linked artifacts:
- Router log excerpt (attached in ticket files).
- Trace and dashboard links (see related_confluence_pages).
- PR revert and hotfix commits: github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-router/commit/7a9b2c and /commit/9d4f1a

Status: Resolved.
